title: E4M3/E5M2 proportional gating + noise-attenuation for FP8 enablement on Hopper
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Enable stable FP8 (E4M3/E5M2) activation for selected Hopper-backed model families using a conservative, proportional gating algorithm plus a lightweight noise-attenuation stage. This ticket covers design, calibration harness changes, telemetry gates, a staged canary, and rollback criteria.

Background: Prior FP8 enablement attempts have shown intermittent downstream accuracy drift at tail-percentile prompts due to per-shard variance and rare outlier activations. Existing fallback strategies are binary (on/off) and lead to either lost cost savings or surprising regressions. We need a smoother activation strategy that preserves most cost/latency benefits while bounding worst-case quality regressions.

Acceptance criteria:
- Proportional gating algorithm implemented in the runtime selector for E4M3/E5M2 that can throttle FP8 activation probability per-shard based on a stability score.
- A noise-attenuation transform (per-layer clamp + moving-median smoothing) added to the calibration pipeline to reduce spiky quantization noise in KVs.
- Calibration job that produces a stability score and recommended initial gating weight per model; artifacts (calibration bundles) stored in S3 and linked from the console.
- Canary plan executed on 5% of hostnames for 48h with golden-seed regression suite; no more than 0.5% end-to-end BLEU/ROUGE degradation vs int8 baseline on critical prompt set.
- Automatic rollback trigger when cross-run z-score of latency/QA metrics exceeds configured thresholds.
- Dashboards and alerts created in Console for the key signals listed below.

Design summary:
1) Proportional gating: compute a per-shard stability_score in [0,1] from calibration traces (quantization mismatch, activation variance, bias estimate). Activation probability P = alpha * stability_score + (1 - alpha)*global_safety. Alpha defaults to 0.8 and is tunable per-model. This enables partial traffic to use FP8 instead of an all-or-nothing switch.
2) Noise-attenuation: during calibration, apply a short-window median filter over KV scale factors per-layer and an outlier clamp at 5 sigma to prevent single-batch noise from driving profile decisions.
3) Calibration harness changes: add synthetic perturbation runs to expose sensitivity to rare tokens (token skew), and compute a bias-corrected MSE metric. Output includes stability_score, recommended alpha, and fallback path.
4) Telemetry & gates: track token-level perplexity delta, human-specified eval set regressions, per-shard quant-variance, tail latency (95/99), and error rate. Create a single canary-gate composite score used by the rollout controller.

Test plan:
- Unit tests for gating math and noise-attenuation transforms.
- Local golden-suite runs against small models to verify no regression on the 1000 prompt regression set.
- Clustered calibration sweep across model family (n=20) to generate stability score distribution.
- Shadow traffic run for 24h with progressive increase to 10% traffic; collect metrics and compare to baseline.
- Final canary 5% production traffic for 48h with automatic rollback enabled.

Rollback & fail-safes:
- If composite gate score crosses rollback threshold, controller immediately demotes FP8 probability to 0 for affected shards and triggers incident.
- Fallback models: INT8 baseline and small-quantized variants are available.
- We will run a nightly reconcilation job that re-calibrates stability scores and records drift trends.

Open decisions & trade-offs:
- Alpha default (0.8) chosen to bias toward enabling FP8; trade-off is potential increased regressions for some models.
- We will not pursue fully dynamic per-request switching in this phase due to complexity; gating is per-shard per-minute.
- Whether to include per-customer override in V1 is TBD (blocked on legal review for enterprise contracts).

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Proportional+Gating+for+FP8
- Calibration harness repo (GitHub): https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-calib/tree/feature/proportional-gating
- Golden regression suite (Drive): https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1GOLDENSEED-REGRESSION
- Console dashboard (draft): https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/fp8-gating-canary

Risks:
- Edge-case prompt distributions could still produce unnoticed degradations—mitigated with expanded golden seed and synthetic perturbations.
- Telemetry noise could cause flapping; mitigated with hysteresis and per-shard smoothing.

Next steps:
- Implement gating math and unit tests (owner: Arjun).
- Add noise-attenuation transforms to calibration pipeline (owner: Priya Rao).
- Hook calibration outputs into deployment selector and add dashboard panels (owner: Platform Observability).
- Plan canary window and schedule PRDs with Solutions/PM.
